title: Money Already Standing to a Policyholder on the Premium Account When Premium Is Returned
content:
Money the plan has already given back, or money already standing to the policyholder on a premium account under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies, is deducted when premium is returned, so that nothing is given back twice.

*What is deducted where a return has already been paid on the policy's premium account?* The amount already returned.

*What is deducted where no return has yet been paid on the policy's premium account and the money received on it exceeds the premium charged on it?* The amount by which the money received exceeds the premium charged.

*What is deducted where neither of those holds?* Nothing is deducted.

### Points of judgement

The first case turns only on whether a return has already been paid on that policy's premium account. Where one has, the amount already returned is the deduction, and the money received against the premium charged does not come into it.

The second case is reached only where no return has yet been paid on the account. It then turns on the money received on that account measured against the premium charged on it, and the deduction is the excess of the one over the other, never the whole of either.

Where no return has been paid and the money received does not exceed the premium charged, nothing is deducted.

### Hypothetical figures

Where a return of 55.00 has already been paid on the premium account, the deduction is 55.00.

Where no return has been paid, 400.00 has been received on the account and 355.80 has been charged on it, the money received exceeds the premium charged by 44.20, and that is the deduction.

Where no return has been paid, 300.00 has been received and 355.80 charged, the money received does not exceed the premium charged and nothing is deducted.
